explanation: No clear single theme: fires on assorted tokens in lists of symbols/character classes (punctuation, regex special characters), Go import strings like "testing", part numbers, 'Terms and Conditions', and scattered prose words. Somewhat stronger in symbol-heavy or code contexts, but many top hits are unrelated ordinary words.

Strongest on the Go 'package' keyword that starts a file after license/build-tag comments; otherwise fires moderately on miscellaneous tokens in programming Q&A prose and code (e.g. 'as' in Python with-open, 'of', 'key', 'decoder'), plus scattered unrelated tokens.
Fires at full strength only on a '0' digit inside a long run of zeros (e.g. '0000000' in numbers/timestamps); everything else is very weak (≤12%) and scattered across unrelated subword tokens.

Fires on the first item of an enumerated list, i.e. a token right after an opener like '(', 'for', 'such as', '—', or 'including' that begins a series of comma-separated items (e.g. '(food, water...', 'MMP-1, -2', 'IL10, IL12', 'flights, restaurants'). Moderate for other items or list starts that are weaker; weak elsewhere.

Fires in scientific/news expository prose at the point after an introductory clause or discourse connective where the main claim begins: commas after 'In fact', 'Indeed', 'However', 'Furthermore', after a background clause, and tokens like 'a (growing number)', 'of' in 'a number of', 'new research'. Strongest on such clause-boundary commas in biomedical abstracts.

Mixture: strongly on 'even' in negated emphatic constructions ('didn't even', 'never even', 'not even'); also on 'percent'/'%' after small quantities ('just 1 percent', 'less than 2%'), on 'pone'/'pgen' in PLoS citation keys '[@pone.', and on miscellaneous tokens (URL '/library', legal-document asterisks).

Mostly fires on tokens inside code (string literals, identifiers like 'User', 'ThreadPool', 'menuItem', 'remote_user') and on long whitespace padding in legal case captions after party names; also some prose tokens. No coherent single trigger beyond structured/code-like text.

Diffuse: fires on assorted content words and function words in mid-sentence positions (e.g. 'able' in 'be able to', 'you', 'total', 'former', 'understanding') in prose, often spammy/low-quality web text, and occasionally code tokens. No predictable trigger.

Mixture: fires on the '0' of a year range in copyright headers ('2005-2008'), on indentation/whitespace after '$.ajax({', on opening quote of YAML/JS values, and on the first subword of proper names (especially non-English/transliterated names like 'Manasseh', 'Bhagavata', 'Hefei', 'Bulger').

Fires on word-initial subword pieces starting with 'd' that begin a longer word or acronym: 'DM' (diabetes mellitus/DMH/DMRC), 'des'/'dif'/'dé' prefixes in Romance languages, 'dec'+'ou' in 'decoupled', 'DR'(AM/HLA-DR), 'dys', 'dp'. Strength depends on the token being a D-initial prefix fragment rather than a whole word.

Fires on connecting tokens in fixed boilerplate and range/list structures: the hyphen in copyright year ranges ('2007-2019'), 'along' in GPL 'along with this program', 'to' in param docs and 'Xth to Yth', commas between function parameters or list items. Essentially tokens joining two parallel elements, strongest in license/copyright boilerplate.

Fires on the first token of rarer multi-token names/words that are being split: CJK byte-fragments, 'Shiite', 'Kurdish', 'TripAdvisor', 'AsyncTask', 'StringBuilder', 'PROCUREMENT', 'clearTimeout', 'Seinfeld'. Roughly a 'start of a distinctive named entity or identifier' detector, mixed across domains.

Fires on the opening brace '{' (often with following newline) or first indentation that begins a class, namespace, or function body in C-like code (Java, C#, PHP, JS, ObjC, C++), and on the indentation of the first line inside a body. Prose activations are weak.

Fires on blank-line/newline tokens marking a section break: after field declarations before a constructor in Java classes (indentation before 'public'), and after the end of a question ('?\n\n' before 'A:') in Q&A text. Weaker for ordinary paragraph breaks in news or headers.
